question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹540 for a period of 4 years at the rate of 2% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total effective simple interest rate for 4 years = Rate × Time

Effective Rate = 2% × 4 = 8%

This means 8% of the Principal amounts to the total Simple Interest.

⇒ 8% of P = 540

⇒ P = (540 × 100) ÷ 8 = 6750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 

 
 
 P = ?
 
 
 SI = ₹540
 
 Rate = 2% p.a.
 Time = 4 years
 
 Total SI = 2% × 4 = 8% of P

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹540

Rate of Interest (R) = 2% per annum

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 540 = (P × 2 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 540 = (P × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (540 × 100) ÷ 8

⇒ P = 54000 ÷ 8

⇒ P = 6750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The final amount is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + SI, which can also be written as A = P[1 + (RT ÷ 100)].

Direct Formulas for Rate and Time

You can easily find missing variables by rearranging the base SI formula: R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) and T = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R).

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is always calculated on the original principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.
